reviewed_pages.scope: Whole original summary reviewed: explicit phoneme symbols and cluster variables are class notation, not lexical forms. Source Chitwan/Tanahun variation and vowel-length/noncontrastiveness retained as source context.

Whole original reviewed. Historical -o and current -ə describe adjective word endings without separate morpheme function; retained as class context. Other English morphology summaries contain no quoted target forms.

Original confirms -e purposive marker and -ikun with both sequential-converb and complementation functions. Other sentence/discourse summaries contain English examples only; no unrecorded target words.

Full original reviewed: comparative phonology prose has no lexical tokens. Footnote explicitly says secondary sources underpin this section; preserve attribution rather than treating all comparison languages as new Darai fieldwork.

All 48 pronoun cells reviewed against original; six Darai cells and 42 foreign comparison cells kept separately with exact person-number headers. Rajbanshi private wedge symbols resolved to ʌ; extra h in tʌmʰha literal. Pronoun-initial letters in commentary are sound classes, not separate morphemes.

Original confirms Darai -l past and -t non-past. Foreign -l/-k comparison remains in preserved lines22–25, with -l~n Kumal, -cʰ multi-language and -c Rajbanshi scoped controls. Possessive-suffix discussion supplies no specific suffix shapes. No inferred cognate or donor edges.

Previously viewed whole original during table preparation. All 56 tense cells, including 18 positive marker attestations and blank/dash absences, compared with row and column headings. Darai has only -l past and -t non-past; no future check. Bote past-j parenthesized check retained. Feminine -i and source Sanskrit -ika historical claim preserved; n-/b- class discussion not silently assigned as Darai lexical forms.

All 24 negative-table cells and areal comparison prose reviewed. Darai nai/nidzə co-listing is source grouping, not evidence of free variation; later expansion must preserve both without automatic variant edge. Darai dzʰun distinct from Bote dzʰin and Majhi dzun. Danuwar prefix column literally -nəi retains inconsistent hyphen orientation. Empty cells are absence controls.

Both surface and segmented verb witnesses match original, including nasal ĩ and simultaneous 1PL/3SG.H/PL agreement labels. Subject versus object roles come from explicit source prose and translation; do not collapse multiple person labels into a single coherent subject tag. Remaining prose has no new quoted target forms.

Original confirms ke-, r, k and l- as explicit Darai morphemes, with source person-number restrictions on genitives and past/perfect function for l-. Literal trailing hyphens preserved despite suffix analysis. Isolated j/w are phonological classes, not lexical forms; genealogical argument remains attributed context.

All eight quoted units reviewed. Darai baṭə, -səb, possibility b, and kono separated from historical eastern baṭi and Bihari/Oriya/Hindi possessive comparisons. Explicit possibility-versus-future distinction retained. Genitive/relative vowel classes are context, and proposed genealogy is not an accepted lexical edge.
Whole original classification figure and research suggestions reviewed; no lexical evidence. Proposed Darai subgrouping stays an attributed scholarly claim, not a registry change.
